[1] warranty.md > Out of warranty
## Registration

Registration is optional. A customer who registers a product on the online store, with the order
number and the serial number, is contacted directly if the company issues a safety notice for
that model, and does not need to produce a receipt for a claim. Registration does not extend the
warranty period.

## Out of warranty

Products outside their warranty period, and declined claims, can be repaired by the Repair Center
for a fee. The customer is quoted before any work is done and can decline the quote, in which
case the product is returned at the customer's shipping cost. The bench fee of $25.00 pays for
the inspection and the quote, and is charged whether or not the customer goes ahead with the
repair. The Repair Center's own manual
describes the fee schedule and the shop procedures.

## Safety notices

If a defect is found that affects safety, the company notifies registered owners directly,
publishes a notice on the website and offers a free repair or replacement regardless of warranty
status. The last such notice was in February 2021 for a batch of Beacon 400 battery springs; it
is closed.

Manual
Last updated: September 8, 2026 Owner: Walt Brannigan, Head of Repairs
This manual is for the technicians at the Repair Center, 1180 Downsville Pike, Dock B,
Hagerstown. It covers intake, the bench rules, and the service procedures for every current

Intake
Every lantern that comes through Dock B gets a repair ticket before anyone touches it. Ticket
numbers are RT- followed by five digits (for example RT-20931) and are issued by the intake
terminal. The ticket records the customer's name, the order number if there is one, the
model, the serial number from the base plate, the fault as the customer described it, and the
condition on arrival, including scratches, dents and missing parts. Photograph every lantern
from the front and from the base before you open the box flaps the rest of the way.
Each ticket gets a coloured tag tied to the bail or handle:

Each ticket gets a coloured tag tied to the bail or handle:
Red tag: warranty repair. The claim already has a WC- number from Customer Service.
No charge to the customer, and the return shipping is on us.
Yellow tag: paid repair. The customer has agreed to the bench fee and to an estimate
for parts.
Green tag: Second Light refurbishment. These are returns and trade-ins being rebuilt
for the refurbished shelf. There is no customer waiting, so they are worked after red
and yellow tags.
The bench fee for a paid repair is $25.00 plus parts at the catalogue price of the part. The fee
is waived under warranty. If a yellow-tag repair turns out to need parts beyond the estimate
by more than $10, stop and have Customer Service call the customer before you continue. Do
not guess at what the customer would want.

Turnaround for a paid repair is 10 business days from the day the lantern arrives at Dock B,
counting the arrival day as day zero. Warranty repairs are worked in the same queue and
carry the same target. If a part is on backorder, the ticket is flagged "waiting on parts" and
the customer is emailed on the third day of waiting and every five business days after that.
Fuel lanterns arrive with fuel in them more often than you would think, whatever the
packing instructions say. Drain any fuel lantern over the drain tray at the intake bench
before it goes to a shelf, and log the drained fuel in the fuel room book. A lantern that smells
of kerosene when the ticket says white gas gets a note on the ticket; it changes what you look
for.
Bench rules
1. Every repaired lantern runs for 30 minutes on the bench before it goes back to the
customer. LED lanterns run on high for the first 10 minutes and low for the rest. Fuel
lanterns run on high for the whole 30 minutes on the vented bench, bench 3 or bench 4
only. Record the start and end time on the ticket. A lantern that fails the burn-in goes
back to the start of the procedure, not to the shipping bench.

Northstar Dual-Fuel (LS-ND2)

The Northstar is our most repaired product by a wide margin, which is a function of how
many we sell and of how it is used, not of any weakness. Nearly every Northstar fault is one
of four things: a clogged generator, a dry pump cup, a torn mantle, or the wrong fuel. Ask
about the fuel first. The Northstar burns Clearburn white gas or unleaded gasoline. It does
not burn kerosene, and a tank that has had kerosene in it will have a varnished generator
and a sticky check valve. That is a paid repair even inside the warranty period.
Tools for the Northstar bench: 11 mm and 13 mm open-ended wrenches, the generator
wrench (part T-ND2, the thin 9 mm one with the bent handle), a small flat screwdriver, the
pump cup oil bottle, a nylon brush, and the torque driver set to 2.5 N·m for checking.
Generator tube replacement
The generator (part G-GEN2) is the tube that runs up through the burner and carries fuel
from the tank to the mantles. Signs of a bad generator are a weak yellow flame that will not
steady, pulsing light, and a tank that holds pressure but will not deliver it. The part is
$13.00, so a typical generator replacement on a yellow tag comes to $38.00 with the bench
fee.

[4] customer-service-playbook.md > Scenario 2: a Sentinel 1000 Pro that stopped charging
### Scenario 1: a return just outside the window

On Monday, October 12, 2026, a customer emails about order LS-2026-008316, a Beacon 600 ordered
on August 20 and delivered on August 29. She wants to return it because she bought a Sentinel 1000
instead. Forty days from August 29 is October 8, so the window closed four days before she wrote.
The agent replies with RET-01, adjusted: the lantern is unused and boxed, so the agent offers,
with the shift lead's okay, an exchange toward the Sentinel 1000 as a one-time courtesy, with the
12% restocking fee waived because it is an exchange. The customer accepts. The agent issues
RA-121877, offers the $8.50 prepaid label, and notes the courtesy on the ticket. The exchange
difference is charged when the Beacon 600 arrives at Hagerstown.

### Scenario 2: a Sentinel 1000 Pro that stopped charging

On Thursday, September 3, 2026, a customer calls about a Sentinel 1000 Pro bought on June 14,
2025, order LS-2025-002210. It no longer charges from the wall or the solar top. The lantern is
inside its 5-year warranty, but the battery pack is inside its own 1-year battery warranty only
until June 14, 2026, which has passed. The agent opens warranty claim WC-030517 anyway, because
the fault may be the charging circuit rather than the pack, and explains that the Repair Center
will decide within 5 business days. On September 8 Walt Brannigan's team finds a failed charge
controller, which is a manufacturing defect covered by the 5-year warranty, and repairs it at no
charge under repair ticket RT-20931. The lantern ships back on September 11. Had the fault been
the pack alone, the agent would have quoted a paid pack replacement instead.

[5] returns-policy.md > Restocking fee
### Final sale, no returns

The following are sold as final sale and cannot be returned or exchanged:

- Clearance items marked "Last Light" on the product page, the price tag or the receipt.
- Custom-engraved items, including engraved Heritage No. 7 lamps and engraved gift sets.
- Gift cards, physical and electronic.
- Opened fuel: Clearburn White Gas (LS-FUEL1), Clearburn Lamp Oil (LS-OIL1) and kerosene.
- Mantles (M-21), wicks (W-78), chimneys (CH-7), globes and other consumables once the
  packaging has been opened.

Unopened fuel and unopened consumables may be returned under the ordinary rules, but fuel cannot
be mailed back; it must be brought to a showroom.

## Restocking fee

A restocking fee of 12% of the item price applies to any opened, non-defective item. "Opened"
means the factory seal or shrink wrap has been broken, or the item has been removed from its
inner packaging. An item returned in an unopened, sealed box carries no fee.

The fee is waived when:

- The return is an exchange for another item of equal or greater value.
- The item is defective, as confirmed by customer service or the Repair Center.
- The wrong item was shipped, or the item does not match its product page.
- The customer is a Beacon-tier Lumen Rewards member and the return is their first of the
  calendar year.

The fee is calculated on the price paid after discounts and before tax and shipping. On a Beacon
600 (LS-600) bought at $79.99, the fee is $9.60. On a Sentinel 1000 Pro (LS-1000P) at $219.99,
the fee is $26.40. The fee is never charged on a showroom return made within 7 days of purchase
with the receipt.

## Return shipping

The customer pays return shipping unless the item is defective or the wrong item was shipped.
Customers may use any carrier they like and are responsible for the package until it arrives
at the Hagerstown warehouse; the Customer Service team recommends tracking and insurance on
anything over $100.

A prepaid return label is offered on every mailed return for a flat $8.50, deducted from the
refund. The label is a UPS Ground label addressed to the warehouse and is good for 14 days from
the day it is issued. One label covers one package; a return of more than one package needs a
label per package, each at $8.50.

When the item is defective or the wrong item was shipped, the prepaid label is free and no
restocking fee applies.
